questions.q: $f(x)=\left(20-x^4\right)^{1 / 4} \quad$ for $\quad 0 < x < \sqrt{5}$, then $f \left(f \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)is equal to$
questions.solution:
We have,
$\begin{aligned} f(x) & =\left(20-x^4\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \\ f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) & =\left(20-\frac{1}{16}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}=\left(\frac{319}{16}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \\ f\left[f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right] & =f\left[\left(\frac{319}{16}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\right] \\ & =\left(20-\frac{319}{16}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{16}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{1}{2}=2^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The function $f: R \rightarrow R$ is defined by $f(x)=3^{-x}$. Observe the following statements of it
I. $f$ is one-one
II. $f$ is onto
III. $f$ is a decreasing function
Out of these, true statement are
questions.solution:
Since, $f: R \rightarrow R$ such that $f(x)=3^{-x}$.
Let $y_1$ and $y_2$ be two elements of $f(x)$ such that $\begin{aligned}$& y_1=y_2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 3^{-x_1}=3^{-x_2} \Rightarrow x_1=x_2 \\
&
\end{aligned} Since, if two images are equal, then their elements are equal, therefore it is one-one function
Let y=3^{-x} On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\frac{d y}{d x}=-3^{-x} \log 3 < 0$ for every value of $x\therefore$ It is decreasing function
$\therefore$ Statement I and II are true.

questions.solution:
We have,
$e^{f(x)}=\frac{10+x}{10-x}f(x)=\log \frac{10+x}{10-x}$
Given that $f(x)=k f\left(\frac{200 x}{100+x^2}\right)\Rightarrow \quad \log \frac{10+x}{10-x}=k \cdot \log \left\{\frac{10+\frac{200 x}{100+x^2}}{10-\frac{200 x}{100+x^2}}\right\}=k \log \left\{\frac{1000+10 x^2+200 x}{1000+10 x^2-200 x}\right\}=k \log \left\{\frac{x^2+100+20 x}{x^2+100-20 x}\right\}=k \log \left\{\frac{(x+10)^2}{(10-x)^2}\right\}=2 k \log \frac{10+x}{10-x}\Rightarrow \quad \log \frac{10+x}{10-x}=2 k \log \frac{10+x}{10-x}\therefore \quad 2 k=1 \Rightarrow k=\frac{1}{2}=0.5$

questions.solution: We have, $f(x)=x^2+3 x-3\Rightarrow \quad y=x^2+3 x-3\Rightarrow \quad y=x^2+3 x-3+\frac{9}{4}-\frac{9}{4}\Rightarrow y=\left(x+\frac{3}{2}\right)^2-\frac{21}{4}\Rightarrow \quad y+\frac{21}{4}=\left(x+\frac{3}{2}\right)^2\Rightarrow \quad x+\frac{3}{2}=\sqrt{y+\frac{21}{4}} \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{y+\frac{21}{4}}-\frac{3}{2}\Rightarrow f^{-1}(y)=\sqrt{y+\frac{21}{4}}-\frac{3}{2}\Rightarrow f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x+\frac{21}{4}}-\frac{3}{2}=g(x)$ (given) Minimum value of $f^{-1}(x)$ is $\frac{-3}{2}\therefore \quad \alpha=-\frac{3}{2}\therefore \quad x=\alpha+\frac{5}{2}=-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{5}{2}=\frac{2}{2}=1$ Now, $g(x)=\sqrt{x+\frac{21}{4}}-\frac{3}{2}\Rightarrow \quad g^{\prime}(x)=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x+\frac{21}{4}}}$ at $\quad x=1, g^{\prime}(x)=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{1+\frac{21}{4}}}=\frac{1}{5}$

questions.solution: Let $x$ and $y$ be any two elements in the domain $(Z)$, such that $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)\ldots$ (i) Differentiating above expression w.r.t ' $y$ ', keeping $x$ constant, we get $f^{\prime}(x+y)=f^{\prime}(y)$ Let $y=0 \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x+0)=f^{\prime}(0)$ and Assume $f^{\prime}(0)=K\therefore \quad f^{\prime}(x)=K$ Integrating on both sides, we get $f(x)=K x+C\{C \rightarrow \text { integration constant }\}\ldots$ (ii) Now putting $x=y=0$ in Eq. (i), we get $f(0+0)=f(0)+f(0) \Rightarrow f(0)=2 f(0)$ or $f(0)=0$ Let $x=0$, from Eq. (ii) $f(0)=K \times 0+C \text { or } 0=0+C \text { or } C=0\therefore \quad f(x)=k x$ Case (i) If $k>0$, then $f(x)$ is strictly increasing. Case (ii) If $k < 0$, then $f(x)$ is strictly decreasing So, function is injective Also $f(x)$ where every element in the codomain is a valid output of the function i.e., range is equal to codomain. So, function is surjective also. Therefore, there are two bijective functions.

questions.q:
Let $f: R \to R$ be a periodic function such that $f\left(T + x\right) = 1 + {\left[1 - 3f\left(x\right) + 3{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{2} - {\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{3}\right]}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}$ where $T$ is a fixed positive number, then period of $f \left(x\right) is

$
questions.solution:
Given : $f\left(T + x\right) = 1 + {\left[{ \left($1 - f \left(x\right)\right)}^{3}\right]}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}$

$= 1 + \left(1 - f\left(x\right)\right)$

$⇒ f\left(T + x\right) + f\left(x\right) = 2$ ... (1)

$⇒ f\left(2T + x\right) + f\left(T + x\right) = 2$ ... (2)

Subtracting (1) from (2)

$f\left(2T + x\right) - f\left(x\right) = 0$

$f\left(2T + x\right) - f\left(x\right) = 0$

Also, $T$ is positive therefore period of $f\left(x\right) = 2T$

$= sec \left(log \left($x + $\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}\right)\right) \left($∵ $sec\left(- \theta\right) =$sec \left(\theta\right)\right)$

questions.q: If $2\text{f}\left(\text{xy}\right) = {\left(\text{f}\left(\text{x}\right)\right)}^{y} + {\left(\text{f}\left(\text{y}\right)\right)}^{x}$ for all $\text{x,}\text{y} \in \text{R}$ and $\text{f} \left($1\right) = 3,$ then the value of $\mathop{Σ}_{\text{r} =$1}^{1 0} $\text{f} \left(\text{r}\right)is equal to
questions.solution:
From given functional equation, $2\text{f}\left(\text{xy}\right) = {\left(\text{f}\left(\text{x}\right)\right)}^{y} + {\left(\text{f}\left(\text{y}\right)\right)}^{x} , ∀ \text{x,}\text{y} \in \text{R}$

putting $\text{y} = 1$,

$2\text{f}\left(\text{x}\right) = \text{f}\left(\text{x}\right) + {\left(\text{f}\left(\text{1}\right)\right)}^{x}$

$\text{f}\left(\text{x}\right) = {3}^{x}$

$∴ \mathop{Σ}_{\text{r} = 1}^{1 0} \text{f} \left(\text{r}\right) = \mathop{Σ}_{\text{r} = 1}^{1 0} {3}^{r} = \dfrac{3 \left({3}^{1 0} -1\right)}{3 - 1} = $\dfrac{3}{2} \left({3}^{1 0} -$1\right)$

questions.q: If $f  \left(x\right) = sinx + cosx$ and $g\left(x\right) = x^{2} - 1$, then g\l$left(f\left($x\right)\right)$ is invertible in the domain$
questions.solution:
Given, $f\left(x\right) = sinx + cosx$

$g\left(x\right) = x^{2} - 1$

$g\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = {\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{2} - 1 = {\left(sinx + cosx\right)}^{2} - 1 = sin2x$

But $sin2x$ is invertible in a case when $- \dfrac{\pi}{2} \le 2x \le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

⇒ $- \dfrac{\pi}{4} \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.solution:
$f^{'}\left(\text{x}\right) = 2 - \text{cos x} ∀ \text{x} \in \text{R⇒}$ one - one,

and $g^{'}\left(\text{x}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}x^{- 2 / 3} > 0 ⇒$one - one

Since, both $g$ and $f$ are one - one, hence, $gof$ is also one - one.

Range of $f \left(x\right)$ is \left(- \infty, \infty\right)$as $f \left(x\right)$ is continuous and $f \left($x\right) \to $\pm \inftyas $x \to $\pm \infty.

Also, since domain of g\left($x\right)$ is $R$, $y = x^{\dfrac{1}{3}}$

$⇒ x = y^{3}$

$⇒ y^{3} \in \left(- \infty, \infty\right)$

$⇒ y \in \left(- \infty, \infty\right)$

$⇒$ Range of $g \left($x\right)$ is also $R$.

$

questions.q: If $f$ is a function defined as $f( x ) = x^{2} - x + 5, f: ( \dfrac{1}{2}, \infty ) \to ( \dfrac{19}{4}, \infty ),$ and $g( x )$ is its inverse function, then $g^{'}  \left(7\right) is equal to$
questions.solution:
$f ⁡ \left(\text{x}\right) = x^{2} - \text{x} + 5$

$f^{'} ( x ) = 2x - 1$
$⇒ for \text{y} = 7 \text{,} \text{x} > \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ 7 = x^{2} - \text{x} + 5$

$⇒ x^{2} - \text{x} - 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(\text{x} - 2\right) \left(\text{x} + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \text{x} = - \text{1, 2}$

$⇒x = 2$ (as $x = - 1$ is rejected)

$Iff\left(x\right) & g\left(x\right)areinverseofeachother,g\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = x$

$⇒ g^{'}\left(f\left({x}_{}\right)\right) . \left(f^{'}\left(x\right)\right) = 1$

substituting $x = 2$ in this equation,

we get, $g^{'} ( f ( 2 ) ) . f^{'} ( 2 ) = 1$

$⇒ g^{'} ( f ( 2 ) ) = \dfrac{1}{f^{'} ( 2 )}$
$g^{'} ( 7 ) = \dfrac{1}{2 ( 2 ) - 1}$

$= \dfrac{1}{3} ( atx = 2 )$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{3} + cos ⁡ \dfrac{3x}{10}$ for all real $x .$ The least natural number $n$ such that $f\left(10n\pi + x\right) = f\left(x\right)$ for all real values of $x$ is
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{3} + cos ⁡ \dfrac{3x}{10}$

Period of $sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{3} = 6\pi$

Period of $cos ⁡ \dfrac{3x}{10} = \dfrac{20\pi}{3}$

$\left(∵ sin ⁡ a\theta,cos ⁡ a\thetaareperiodicwithperiod\dfrac{2\pi}{\left|a\right|}\right)$

LCM of $\left(6\pi, \dfrac{20\pi}{3}\right) = 60\pi$

Therefore, the period of $f\left(x\right) = 60\pi$

Hence, $n = 6 .$

$= \sin^{2} ⁡ x + \left[$sin ⁡ xcos ⁡ $\dfrac{π}{3} +$cos ⁡ xsin ⁡ $\dfrac{π}{3}\right]$2 + cos ⁡ x \left[cos ⁡ xcos ⁡ \dfrac{π}{3} - sin ⁡ xsin ⁡ \dfrac{π}{3}\right]$

$= \sin^{2} ⁡ x + $\dfrac{\sin^{2} ⁡ x}{4} + \dfrac{3\cos^{2} ⁡ x}{4} +$sin ⁡ xcos ⁡ x . $\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{\cos^{2} ⁡ x}{2} -$sin ⁡ xcos ⁡ $\dfrac{3}{2}

$= $\dfrac{5\sin^{2} ⁡ x}{4} +$5$\dfrac{\cos^{2} ⁡ x}{4} = \dfrac{5}{4}

$∴ gof\left($x\right) = g\left[$f\left($x\right)\right] = g\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right) =$1$ (given)

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{9}^{x}}{{9}^{x} + 3}$ and $f\left(x\right) + f\left(1 - x\right) = 1$ then find value of 2 times $f\left(\dfrac{1}{1996}\right) + \left(\dfrac{2}{1996}\right) + \ldots . . + f\left(\dfrac{1995}{1996}\right) .$
questions.solution:
We have, $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{9}^{x}}{{9}^{x} + 3}$

$∴ f\left(x\right) + f\left(1 - x\right) = 1$

$∴ f\left(\dfrac{1}{1996}\right) + f\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{1996}\right) = 1 . . . \left(i\right)$

$f\left(\dfrac{2}{1996}\right) + f\left(1 - \dfrac{2}{1996}\right) = 1 . . . \left(ii\right)$

and so on $f\left(\dfrac{1995}{1996}\right) + f\left(1 - \dfrac{1995}{1996}\right) = 1 . . . \left(iii\right)$

Adding all the equation we get,

$2\left(f\left(\dfrac{1}{1996}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{2}{1996}\right) + \ldots + f\left(\dfrac{1995}{1996}\right)\right) = 1995$

$⇒ f\left(\dfrac{1}{1996}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{2}{1996}\right) + \ldots + f\left(\dfrac{1995}{1996}\right) = 997 . 5$
